Our research
The Jepps Lab at the University of Copenhagen is an exciting, highly translational vascular biology group where myography and cardiovascular physiology meet cutting-edge mass spectrometry and proteomics to uncover new mechanisms driving hypertension and vascular inflammation. By combining functional measurements of arterial tone and remodeling with deep proteomic profiling, the lab moves seamlessly from identifying disease-associated proteins and pathways to testing their physiological relevance in experimental models. What makes the lab particularly attractive is its clear ambition to translate discovery into patient benefit: findings from vascular physiology and proteomics are being used to understand how inflammation contributes to hypertension and to identify interventions that can be tested clinically. This translational pipeline is already becoming reality with colchicine, where mechanistic work on vascular inflammation and remodeling has progressed from experimental studies to the COHERENT randomized clinical trial investigating low-dose colchicine in patients with hypertension. For researchers who want to work across molecular discovery, quantitative proteomics, vascular physiology and clinical translation—and ultimately see laboratory findings move all the way toward clinical trials—the Jepps Lab offers a uniquely integrated and ambitious environment.
Profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:
Essential Experience And Skills

  * You have a PhD in health sciences.
  * You are highly experienced with a substantial track record in performing and analysing mass spectrometry from different tissues, especially arteries – both rodent and human.
  * You have an active interest in vascular physiology and vascular inflammation.
  * You have extensive experience working with animals, particularly rodents, both in vivo and ex vivo.
  * Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams.
  * Competent with spatial proteomics and confocal microscopy.
  * A strong track record of using Perseus, R and similar software’s for bioinformatic analyses.
  * A teaching portfolio that spans several years of teaching within cardiovascular physiology.
  * Excellent English skills written and spoken
  * Experience of supervising Master’s and Bachelor students in research projects.
  * Ability to multitask to push forward collaborative projects at the same time as undertaking your main research project.
Desirable Experience And Skills

As part of my vocational training at Dr. Notghi, we had to develop and manage a complete phase of a clinical study for a chosen medicinal product. Our chosen product was the Manuka-honey-based eye drops of our mock Startup company, ApiVision. The project included initial steps, such as SWOT analysis and precise goal definition, as well as regulatory strategy development (with the final goal of gaining central EU market access), budget planning, resource planning, and of course, in-depth planning of the phase III clinical study. As part of the study itself, the specification book (Lastenheft), functional specification document (Pflichtenheft), specific work packages, clinical study design, quality assurance measures, risk analysis and a precise calendar with tasks, functions, resources and budget (using MS Project) were created.
My focus was the regulatory affairs aspect of the project. As part of it, I had to develop the complete strategy for the centralized European marketing approval, as well as the entire work packages related to it (pre-submission interaction and consultation with the EMA, determination of eligibility for the centralized procedure, generation of the CTD dossier, communication with the EMA, preparation for possible inspections during the approval process, etc.).
In addition, as part of the phase III clinical trial, I developed the strategy to obtain permission to conduct the study in Germany (clinical study design, communication with the BfArM and the ethics committee, preparation of submission documents, etc.). Weniger anzeigen
